P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Under BNR Regulation 42/2022 (as amended in 2025), cross-border payments such as exports and offshore service contracts are permitted through authorised channels with documentation. BNR's 2025 directive on who may transact in foreign currency covers service providers earning foreign currency from abroad. However, quoting or charging foreign-currency prices to Rwandan residents without BNR authorisation is banned, with fines of RWF 5m–10m for pricing and 50–100% of the amount for unauthorised transactions. No surrender requirement was found.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Transactions through licensed foreign-currency accounts are among the uses permitted under the 2022 FX regulation, and the 2025 amendment keeps them. Bank-specific requirements were not researched.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Rwanda (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Available: Paddle (not on its exclusion list; software sellers only, each seller reviewed); Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts); Polar (payouts); Whop (payouts); Dodo Payments (sellers); Google Play (developer registration). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

P3_local_gateways.notes: IremboPay (BNR-licensed) accepts MTN MoMo, Airtel Money and cards. Onboarding is not self-serve and requires a business registration certificate, a TIN and owners' IDs, so a registered (RDB) business is needed. Paystack operates in Rwanda with MTN MoMo, Airtel Money and cards. A 2026 guide says onboarding needs RDB registration and an RRA TIN. Paystack's own Rwanda compliance page was blocked (Cloudflare error) or missing (404). A search summary of Paystack's support article described a 'Starter' tier for unregistered sole traders (ID + personal bank account), but the page (support2.paystack.com) returned a Cloudflare 1034 error and was not bypassed. Treat as unconfirmed.

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: Not confirmed. Rwanda is a listed PayPal market but not on the PayPal Payouts list. A relocation blog reportedly lists Rwanda among send-only PayPal countries, but its text could not be retrieved. No 2025–2026 source confirming receiving or withdrawal for Rwandan accounts was found. Xoom (PayPal-owned) handles inbound remittances to MTN wallets, which is separate.

Only the Payouts-list absence is established.

P5_payoneer_wise.question: Payoneer / Wise availability for residents
P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: the standard choice for Rwandan freelancers per a 2026 guide. It provides virtual USD/EUR/GBP receiving details, withdrawal to Rwandan banks takes 2–5 business days, and fees are about USD 1.50–3 per withdrawal (unverified against Payoneer). Wise: Rwanda is NOT on Wise's list of countries whose residents can hold money, even though the same guide recommends Wise.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: An 'individual enterprise' (business in the owner's name) is registered online with the Office of the Registrar General at RDB. The service is immediate and free, and RDB–RRA integration issues a single TIN. Anyone setting up a taxable activity must register. Since Law 011/2026, online businesses face new e-commerce disclosure obligations and reportedly licensing, with a 6-month transition.

L1_registration.notes: The online-business licensing requirement under Law 011/2026 is from press summaries (search result), not captured; the Law's text was not read.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The TIN from the Rwanda Revenue Authority. Business owners are registered for income tax automatically when registering through RDB. Individuals without a business (e.g. property owners, PAYE) register at RRA offices. Turnover under RWF 2m is exempt from income tax.

sources.title: Register for Income Tax — exemption
sources.quote: A person who has an annual turnover of less than two million Rwandan francs (FRW 2,000,0000);

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Resident individuals are taxed on domestic and foreign-source income. Annual PIT on real profit (from 2023): 0% to RWF 720,000, 10% to 1,200,000, 20% to 2,400,000, and 30% above. Small enterprises with turnover of RWF 12,000,001–20,000,000 pay a 3% lump-sum tax on turnover (they can opt out by keeping accounts). Turnover of RWF 2m–12m pays flat amounts, and turnover under RWF 2m is exempt (L2).

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT is 18%. Exports of goods and services are zero-rated. Registration is mandatory when turnover exceeded RWF 20m in the previous fiscal year or RWF 5m in the previous quarter, within 7 days of the period's end. Voluntary registration is possible.

L5_data_protection.answer: Law 058/2021 on personal data protection and privacy: anyone intending to act as a data controller or processor must register with the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA). The transition period ended on 15 October 2023.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Law 011/2026 of 26 February 2026 on competition and consumer protection replaced Law 36/2012. For the first time it sets e-commerce duties: sellers must disclose registration numbers and physical addresses, and digital distance contracts have their own rules. Consumers may withdraw from online purchases within 7 days of receiving the good or service (art. 42).

sources.title: Rwanda: A New Consumer Protection Law for a Modern Marketplace (16 Mar 2026)
sources.quote: a defined right of withdrawal allowing consumers to cancel online purchases within seven days of receiving a good or service (Article 42 of New Competition and Consumer Protection Act).

sources.quote: This Law governs competition and consumer protection and applies to any economic activity carried out by any means which is related to business and has an effect on the consumer or on competition in the Rwandan market.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.notes: The New Times piece and Andersen's article share an author (Andersen Rwanda), so they were not counted as independent. The Gazette text was not read.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) Income tax exemption under RWF 2m turnover, flat tax for RWF 2m–12m, and 3% lump sum for RWF 12m–20m (L2/L3). (2) Exports are zero-rated for VAT (L4). (3) Free, immediate online business registration with an automatic TIN (L1). (4) A 5-year foreign-income PIT exemption for newly resident experts working for KIFC-licensed entities (not relevant to most freelancers).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
